name: g1_turn_in_place
title: Natural 90 deg step-around turn (four footfalls, no yaw rope)
summary: A purpose-designed 90 degree humanoid step-around: two 45 degree increments, each made by right then left swing, for four deliberate footfalls total. Minimum-jerk pelvis/foot yaw, smooth COM transfer, subtle waist lead and arm counter-swing replace the old six-step calibrated staircase. Yaw torque remains zero. It is a 153-dim whole-body sequence and therefore runs through BATON's solo context swap.

ghost.notes: build_step_turn_ghost.py --motion-profile natural --inc 2: exact stance closure, 0/108 infeasible dynamics frames, 0.21 torque ratio, 0.01 speed ratio. Validator WARNs only because a sequence has no recorded edit baseline.

baton.notes: solo_swap: _wr_turn_swap replaces every world._wr_* deploy field with the turner's context for the turn segment; blend + warm loop are skipped while in the turn; cold-hidden both ways. Continuous-turn + decel-stop (TURN_TO_DEG/TURN_DECEL_DEG) arrests the spin. Reliability is fragile in-sequence (the open wall).

train.notes: Trained on a RunPod RTX A4500 (cloud venue); 0.22 rad corridor passes the ankle-CoP authority gate. Foot torsion must match train/deploy.

verification.support: G1 lambda=0.9 weight-bearing balance harness; zero yaw torque; not free-standing
verification.result: The natural four-footfall checkpoint and feasible ghost are packaged, but this new default has no end-to-end certification yet. The 86-90 deg solo and 90.6-95.6 deg 3/3 sequence results belong to the older wr_stepturn/wr_turn90 assets explicitly pinned by turn_solo and walk_turn_walk; they are not evidence for this natural checkpoint.
